title: Make Default asks first and says customers keep their term
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop uses COD as the default and has a term of its own you are thinking of making the default.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • COD is the shop's default for new customers.
  • The shop has its own active term {Term-A}, due 14 days after the invoice date.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-20 Fourteen.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the {Term-A} row.
  2. Click "Make Default for New Customers".
  3. Click "Cancel".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens.
  • Step 2: a confirmation opens titled "Make {Term-A} the default?" with the message "New customers start on {Term-A}. Customers you already have keep their current term." and the buttons "Cancel" and "Make Default".
  • Step 3: the confirmation closes; the "Default" tag stays on COD and no toast shows.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11671 (Story 2, Row menu actions)

  • S2-R5: “"Make Default for New Customers" opens a confirmation titled "Make {name} the default?" with the message "New customers start on {name}. Customers you already have keep their current term." and the buttons "Cancel" and "Make Default".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Make Default chosen | "Make {name} the default?" / "New customers start on {name}. Customers you already have keep their current term." | Confirmation, buttons "Cancel" and "Make Default"”
  • Key Decisions: “Deleting a term asks for confirmation; deactivating, reactivating and making a term the default are confirmed only where the result is not obvious. Delete is permanent and asks first. Deactivate and Reactivate are reversible and act at once with a toast. Make Default confirms, because its effect on existing customers (none) needs saying.”
